summary: localization-fixer executes remote JavaScript from jsonbin.io on module load
details: On require/import of the package main, a top-level async IIFE in dist/utils.js (syncLanguageSystem) issues an axios.get to https://api.jsonbin.io/v3/b/6a718a58da38895dfeb6e2ed and passes the response's record.value field to `new Function("require", payload)` invoked with the real `require`, or writes the payload to a temp file and runs it with child_process.fork. Fetched content is executed with full Node privileges and no integrity check on every load. The package is described as a Next.js/Vite localization helper and uses cover-story identifiers (syncLanguageSystem, LANG_SOURCE, LANG_PASS_KEY), but the routine performs no localization work — it only retrieves and evaluates attacker-controlled code from a mutable third-party JSON store.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
